**My pick: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel, $699 (list $879).** It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W AC output and a LiFePO4 battery, and it's rated 4.5 stars across 1.4K reviews. Talk of the House also named it editor's choice, citing 4,000+ cycles, a 23.8 lb weight and roughly 1-hour wall charging. Its one caveat is that fast charging needs the app. [Buy on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included)

**Other good options by need:**

| Whole-home capacity | BLUETTI Elite 300 + 2×200W (3,014Wh, 2,400W) | $1,599.99 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |

If you're a Costco member, the Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with a solar panel is $899.99 online. [Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html)

**Things to know:**
- **Match capacity to use.** About 1,000Wh covers camping, CPAP and short outages, and a fridge for several hours. For multi-day home backup, look at the 2,000Wh+ kits.
- **Bundles can ship in separate boxes.** Talk of the House notes the Jackery 1000 v2's panels ship separately, so don't worry if they arrive on different days. [Source](https://www.talkofthehouse.com/best-solar-generator-kits-with-panels/)
- **Solar charging is slow.** One 200W panel takes about 6–8 hours of full sun to refill a ~1,000Wh unit, and longer on cloudy days.
- **Check the bundle contents.** Several listings with "solar generator" in the title are power stations only, with panels sold separately (for example, the Walmart EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic listing says "Solar Panel Optional").
- **Prices change.** These are from today's search results, so confirm them at checkout.

If you tell me what you'd power (fridge, CPAP, camping, RV) and your budget, I can narrow this to one.
